summary: ALGODEV-61: new top-level mt5/ package -- S021 as a native MQL5 expert advisor for MT5-only prop firms (FundingPips $10K, The5ers, FundedNext+EA). Layout mirrors a terminal MQL5 folder: shared AlgoCore (Clock tz rules, JsonLog compatible with StrategyLogger records, Sessions/ADR port of engine.py, Sizing port of bot/risk.py, AccountGuard port of bot/account_guard.py, TradeOps) + Strategies/S021_ORB (Levels, event-driven Runtime mirroring decide() cases 1-7 with instant OCO cancel via OnTradeTransaction) + thin EA shell; strategy constants are GENERATED from ORB_BASE (mt5/tools/gen_params.py, refuses to export modifier presets). Python tools: tz rules mirror (tested vs zoneinfo hourly 2019-2027), self-test fixtures from histdata+engine, engine-vs-EA parity on broker bars. Verified: MetaEditor build 6235 compiles all 4 programs 0 errors/0 warnings; S021_SelfTest run inside a real terminal: 9828 checks pass (levels on 72 days incl. both 2025 DST ends); tests/mt5 30 passed. Strategy rules untouched; cTrader bot untouched.

ALGODEV-61 follow-up after the first install on Anton's Mac: install_mac.sh now COPIES by default (the macOS/Wine MT5 does not list EAs behind a symlink; scripts work, EAs do not) and also deploys EA input presets (offline tester, FundingPips eval / master-summer, FTMO) into MQL5/Presets and Profiles/Tester; new one-command deploy (deploy.sh for macOS/Linux, deploy.ps1 for Windows): gen_params, tests/mt5, fixtures, copy, MetaEditor CLI compile with error detection, --watch auto-redeploy. Verified headless under Wine: MetaEditor build 6235 compiles all 4 programs 0/0 (compile path must be relative 'MQL5\\...' without /inc). New mt5/docs/SETUP.md (macOS/Windows/Linux, self-test, offline tester + parity, live/prop setup, troubleshooting). First tester run on the Mac (NSXUSD_HD custom symbol, 2025-03..2026-09, 0.5% risk): 366 trades, net +818.65, PF 1.16, max equity DD 3.99%; self-test on the Mac 9828 passed / 0 failed.

First parity run (Mac tester, NSXUSD_HD 2025-03..2026-09) failed on every day: the EA's anchor open equalled the anchor bar's CLOSE and ADR14 was smaller. Root cause: ImportM1CustomSymbol wrote tick_volume=1, and the Strategy Tester never generates more ticks than a bar's tick volume -> one tick per bar (tester report: ticks == bars), so the EA saw O=H=L=C bars. Import now writes tick_volume=4 (IMPORT_TICK_VOLUME) so '1 minute OHLC' gets all four prices. Parity tool caught it as intended; re-import + re-run pending.

ALGODEV-61: S021 EA vs engine parity PASSES on the offline tester (NSXUSD_HD custom symbol, histdata 2025.03.01-2026.09.30, 574 EA days): exit code 0, 326 match / 198 ea_no_levels / 39 live_only_short_session / 11 both_no_trade, 0 failures. The previous run still failed on 304 days even though the tick_volume=4 re-import had already been done; root cause was NOT the EA: the Strategy Tester keeps its own snapshot of a custom symbol in Tester/bases/<server>/history/<symbol>/*.hcs and refreshes it per history chunk, so only the date range of the last (partial) import was correct and the rest replayed 1-tick O=H=L=C bars. Purging Tester/{bases,cache} fixed it -- tester log now shows 2132464 ticks / 533116 bars (ratio 4.0). On the 326 traded days direction, entry minute, entry price and exit_reason are identical (326/326). P&L: EA mean R/trade +0.0834 vs engine gross +0.0793 (engine net +0.0685 = its modelled spread/commission, which the 0-spread custom symbol has none of); the residual +0.004 R is purely intrabar timing of the time exit -- the EA closes on the first tick of the exit minute (the bar open), the engine on that bar's close. Reference run updated: 365 trades, net +1444.23, PF 1.30, win rate 58.4%, max balance DD 3.11%. Docs: SETUP.md gains the mandatory 'drop the tester snapshot after every re-import' step, a headless import/tester recipe (terminal64.exe /config, no /portable, USER=user so FILE_COMMON resolves) and 4 new troubleshooting rows. No EA logic, no strategy rules and no generated headers changed.

ALGODEV-61: CORRECTION -- the S021 session anchor was one hour late in BOTH live bots every US-DST month. histdata's NSXUSD M1 timestamps are true New York local time (DST-aware), not the fixed UTC-5 the repo assumed, so the engine's naive 09:30 reading has always been the real cash open, while bot/ctrader_orb.py converted broker UTC into Etc/GMT+5 and the EA used a fixed-offset clock -- both anchoring at 10:30 NY in summer. Two independent proofs: (1) IC Markets USTEC M1 (774033 bars, server rule EET_US_DST) matches histdata to ~1.5 pts in winter and is off by exactly 60 min in summer, and the intraday volatility peak sits at the true 09:30 NY in both; (2) histdata alone -- re-stamping it into a genuinely fixed UTC-5 moves the 09:30-15:59 window onto 10:30-16:59 NY, where the last hour is past the cash close and only 345 of 390 bars exist, so every summer session fails min_session_bars=350. The September 2026 analysis that 'confirmed' the fixed clock compared the canonical loader against load_nsxusd_m1_true_dst_local, which (timestamps already being NY) anchors at 08:30 NY, in the premarket -- it tested premarket vs the true open and never tested the late anchor the bots actually ran. Cost of the error on broker bars via the production load_broker_bars (2024-08-16..2026-10-02, 523 trades both ways): late anchor +0.0720 R/trade, +37.65 R, maxDD 11.97 R; true NY open +0.1195 R/trade, +62.50 R, maxDD 6.42 R. Fix: new TZ_EST_US_DST / RULE_EST_US_DST rule in both clocks (Clock.mqh and its Python mirror), gen_params now derives the EA clock from engine.SESSION_TZ and emits S021_CLOCK_TZ_RULE instead of S021_CLOCK_UTC_OFFSET_HOURS, Levels.mqh converts through the rule, parity/fixture tooling re-anchored, ctrader_orb.py switched to SESSION_TZ='America/New_York'. deployment/schedule.yml: S021 cron window widened to '* 13-20 * * 1-5' UTC (the summer anchor 13:30 UTC fell OUTSIDE the old 14-20 window -- the bot would not have woken up for the open) and the position audits moved to 13:25/13:26 UTC so they still run before the earliest possible entry. MT5 tester, USTEC M1, OHLC on M1, 2024.07.09-2026.10.04, 1% risk, deposit 10000: final balance 19822.18 (+98.2%) vs 10014.61 for the late anchor on the 14-month subset at 0.5% -- the old edge was thinner than execution cost and netted zero. EA-vs-engine on the 523 common days: 522/523 same direction, entry price within 1 pt on 522, 0 days where the engine traded and the EA did not, EA +67.75 R vs engine +62.50 R over 533/523 trades (the 10 extra EA trades are earlier days the terminal has history for and the CSV export does not). The single direction disagreement (2026-08-18) is a bid/ask artefact, not a bug: the buy stop triggers on the ask while the export and the engine are bid-only, and that day's high missed the level by 0.02 pts on the bid. Also fixed here: FlushDayRow() in Runtime.mqh now rewrites the day's row instead of appending (an EA reinit produced 8 duplicate rows for 2026-10-05); S021_SelfTest asserted '14:30 UTC is always 09:30 on the strategy clock', which the new anchor makes false in summer -- rewritten to 13:30 UTC in DST, 14:30 UTC in standard time, plus a negative assertion guarding against a regression to the fixed clock; RuleFromName() in the self-test silently mapped unknown rule names to TZ_FIXED and did not know EST_US_DST; deploy.sh step 3 only regenerated self-test fixtures when they were MISSING, so the anchor change left stale expectations on disk and the self-test failed 225 of 9834 checks (exactly the DST-side days of the Sep-Dec 2025 fixture window) -- it now compares fixture mtime against s021_fixtures.py, clock.py, config.py and engine.py and warns that a regenerated e2e history needs a fresh ImportM1CustomSymbol. Verification: tests/mt5 33 passed, full suite 654 passed, MetaEditor 0 errors/0 warnings on all 4 programs, in-terminal self-test 12172 passed / 0 failed (up from 9834 checks: the clock fixture now carries 1419 EST_US_DST cases cross-checked against zoneinfo). NOTE on the previous mt5.jsonl entry (2026-10-05T16:38:55): that 'parity PASSES' result is still valid as a port-fidelity statement but was measured on the OLD late anchor; it proves the EA reproduced the engine, not that the anchor was right. Strategy rules untouched -- ORB_BASE in strategies/orb_intraday/config.py is unchanged, only engine.py's module docstring was corrected.

ALGODEV-61 follow-up, docs only, no behaviour change. config.py's module docstring stated the 2026-09-21 conclusion as fact -- that histdata's timestamps are a fixed UTC-5 clock and that the resulting seasonal anchor drift was deliberate. That is the error itself, written down as confirmed truth, so it was the most dangerous stale text in the repo. Rewritten to say the timestamps are true New York local time, that the 2026-09-21 conclusion was wrong, and that the FROZEN VALUES below are unaffected (the backtest always anchored on the real open; only the live bots were late). ORB_BASE values untouched. SETUP.md: the daily timeline claimed 'all S021 times are fixed in UTC' -- replaced by a New York-anchored table with separate US-DST and standard-time UTC columns, plus the non-obvious consequence that the Kyiv reading stays 16:30 in both seasons (Ukraine and the US shift in the same direction) and only drops to 15:30 during the ~2 weeks a year the two DST calendars disagree, while the broker server clock is a constant 7 h ahead of New York year-round. Also: deploy step 3 now documented as regenerating fixtures on staleness, not just on absence; self-test counts refreshed (9828 -> 12172 total, 5549 -> 6968 clock instants); two troubleshooting rows added, the important one being 'self-test fails on roughly half the days and passes on the rest -> suspect stale fixtures, not the code', which is exactly the trap hit earlier today. README.md: new principle that the strategy session clock is GENERATED from engine.SESSION_TZ so the EA and the backtest cannot drift apart, and that a fixed offset there is a bug rather than a shortcut. Not done here and left for a separate rename: the 'fixed-EST' wording still in bot/orb_config.py, bot/orb_signals.py and the method name _parse_trendbars_fixed_est. tests/mt5 + tests/strategies: 219 passed.

Single-instance lock for the expert, found by analysing the first live day on the corrected New York anchor (2026-10-06). The anchor itself behaved: levels were computed at ts_utc 13:30:10 = 09:30 New York (it used to be 14:30 UTC), and the days.csv deduplication held -- one row for today against eight identical rows for 2026-10-05 written by the previous build. The defect was elsewhere: the EA was attached to TWO charts of the same symbol (USTEC,M1 and USTEC,H1) on the same account, and at 16:30:10 each placed its own full long/short pair -- four resting stops instead of two, orders 1990367176/1990367177 (buy) and 1990367212/1990367214 (sell). The M1 copy sized 0.40 lot at 1.003% risk, the H1 copy -- left running from the day before with the old input -- sized 0.80 lot at 2.006%, so a breakout would have filled 1.2 lot, three times the intended risk. Nothing filled (price reached neither level before the duplicates were pulled at 16:37), and the surviving copy reconciled correctly: day_resolved 'orders were already placed and are gone -- no re-entry'. Two further consequences of doubling, both observed: the copies share one magic and one position label, so each one's OCO cancel and position management can act on the other's orders; and they append to the same JSONL, which silently lost records -- events-2026-10-06.jsonl holds three of the four order lines, positions/S021_2026-10-06_long.jsonl one of two. Fix: new strategy-agnostic AlgoCore/InstanceLock.mqh. OnInit claims a temporary terminal global variable named <prefix>:<login>:<symbol>:<magic> holding the owning chart id; a second chart gets INIT_FAILED with an explicit Expert-log line instead of silently doubling the book. The lock is temporary so it never outlives the terminal, and a lock left by a crashed expert is taken over once ChartSymbol(owner) reports the chart is gone -- restarting is always possible, doubling is not. Skipped under MQL_TESTER. Released in OnDeinit only by the owning chart, so the recompile/parameter-change deinit-init cycle on one chart is unaffected. Docs: AlgoCore listing in README, a troubleshooting row in SETUP.md, and the EA header now says the one-chart rule is enforced rather than merely requested. tests/mt5: 33 passed; MetaEditor: 0 errors / 0 warnings on all four programs.

New manual-assist script S021_PlaceToday.mq5, for the day the expert refuses to take. Context: on 2026-10-06 the duplicate-instance incident ended with today's four orders cancelled by hand, after which the expert correctly logged day_resolved and would not re-enter (Runtime.mqh case 6, gate at line 719: 'is there an order in history with my magic and today's comment prefix'). The obvious workaround -- give the expert a second magic number so the day looks fresh -- was rejected, and rightly: magic is the key the daily risk cap and the account guard count by, so a second magic is a second identity on one account whose trades are invisible to the risk already spent. Instead the override is explicit and human: a script, run on demand, that reuses the expert's own code (S021ComputeLevels, SessionsBuild, SizingLotsForRisk/NormalizeVolumeForSymbol/NormalizePrice) so the numbers cannot drift from the EA or the backtest, and places with the EXPERT'S magic and comment so the running EA adopts the orders on its next cycle and manages them normally -- OCO cancel, attached SL, cutoff cancel, time exit (cases 3-5). InpPlace defaults to false: the first run only prints now/levels/size. It refuses on its own outside the 09:30-14:29 New York window, when the EA already holds orders or positions for the day, when ADR14 is not computable, and when a level was already touched since the open -- the last one re-implements the EA's LevelAlreadyTouched test (Runtime.mqh:363) so a human cannot talk it into an entry the backtest never had. Note for future scripts: S021_PCT is private to Runtime.mqh; the shared percent constant is ALGO_PCT in AlgoCore/GeneratedCore.mqh. Docs: new SETUP.md section 7.1, script listed in README, and a live-setup point that one chart only is now enforced. Also corrected a false claim in the SETUP.md TL;DR -- it said an attached EA 'is reloaded automatically after recompilation'. It is not: deploy writes the .ex5 from outside, MT5 keeps running the loaded copy, and Navigator Refresh does not touch it. Cost us two round trips today before the old build was spotted still running; the check is a fresh init event. MetaEditor: 0 errors / 0 warnings on all five programs.

ALGODEV-62 phase B: measured the S004 session clock from the M15 data instead of assuming it (run_s004_clock_probe.py -- the European morning holds its clock hour across both the EU and the US DST transitions, 26 transitions x 3 pairs), pinned it as s004_config.SESSION_TZ = Europe/Bucharest = Clock.mqh TZ_EET_EU_DST, and taught gen_params.py to render Strategies/S004_FVG/Params.mqh from S004_INTRADAY so the EA restates no rule by hand. Export is refused if any of the three prop rules is off.

ALGODEV-62 phase C: ported strategies/fvg_mtf.py::run_backtest to MQL5 (Strategies/S004_FVG/Engine.mqh, pure, no orders) and proved it with a self-test that replays Python-made fixtures: 99659 M15 bars on EURUSD and GBPJPY, 1102 trades reproduced one for one (12132 checks, 0 failures). The expectation deliberately keeps the shadow trades outside the Asia window, because they consume their zone and hold the one-position-per-symbol lock. Added mt5/tools/run_selftest.sh, which runs a self-test script headlessly in a throwaway portable terminal (no profiles, experts off) so the terminal that is trading is never touched -- MT5 silently drops a second instance on the same folder.

ALGODEV-62: kept the whole MT5 side under mt5/, like S021. Moved the session-clock probe out of backtest/ into mt5/tools/s004_clock_probe.py (it exists for the EA, next to clock.py and the other mt5 tools) and updated every reference, including the generated Params.mqh comment. Documented the S004 headers, self-test and tools in mt5/README.md. Hardened run_selftest.sh: it matched the sandbox by its unix path, but the wine process reports the windows one, so a leftover terminal survived and MT5 then dropped the new instance and the run timed out.

ALGODEV-62: made the two S004-intraday sizing dials tunable instead of hardcoded. risk_pct is now a field of S004Config, both it and max_trades_per_day are exported as EA input defaults (S004_DEFAULT_*), and their product is checked against the new DAILY_RISK_BUDGET_PCT=2% -- S004 share of the firm -5% daily limit -- so an impossible pair cannot be exported. Added run_s004_risk_grid.py, which measures the cap x risk grid by busts per 3 years: the budget edge is a cliff (cap 2 goes 3.0 -> 7.1 -> 32.8 busts at 0.50/1.00/1.50%). The default stays 2 x 1.00% per the maintainer. Engine regression and the MQL5 self-test still pass unchanged.

Exit-time question answered and closed: NO modifier added, the frozen session_close 15:59 New York stays. Anton asked why the EA does not hold to the prop firm's day boundary instead, since the daily drawdown resets there anyway. New read-only script backtest/run_s021_exit_time.py replays ONLY the exit on the same broker bars -- levels, ADR14, direction and entry come from the frozen ORB_BASE run and are not recomputed, so moving session_close cannot contaminate the comparison through ADR14 (which is measured over the session window). Validation: replaying at 15:59 reproduces the engine exactly, +62.50 R both. USTEC broker bars 2024-07-28..2026-10-05, 523 trades. Results per cutoff (sum R / R per trade / stops / maxDD R): 15:59 +62.50 / +0.1195 / 82 / 6.42; 16:59 (broker midnight = the prop day end while US DST is on) +61.76 / +0.1181 / 88 / 6.53; 17:59 +61.77 / 88 / 6.53; 19:59 +67.92 / +0.1299 / 91 / 7.42; 21:59 +59.84 / 99 / 8.83; 23:59 +57.08 / +0.1091 / 101 / 8.88. The proposed prop-boundary exit is simply worse on both axes. The 19:59 bump is noise and was rejected on three independent grounds: its neighbours are worse on both sides (61.77 -> 67.92 -> 59.84, a real effect is monotonic), the paired per-trade delta is +0.0104 R with sd 0.2765, t = +0.86 (16:59 gives t = -0.17), and it is negative on the newest data (2024 +2.91, 2025 +3.02, 2026 -0.50). Mechanism behind the monotone decay: win rate falls 57.7 -> 57.0 -> 55.1 -> 53.7% and stops rise 82 -> 101 as hours are added, because the strategy has no take-profit, the stop keeps its intraday-calibrated distance (0.75 * ADR14 of the 09:30-15:59 window), and after the cash close the position sits exposed in thin liquidity with no way to realise. Separately, holding across the prop day boundary is the one case where the daily-loss limit cannot be defended -- an overnight gap breaches it while nobody is awake. Also recorded, found the morning after: the days.csv row an EA writes for a day it joined mid-flight carries the trade but ZERO levels (2026-10-06 shows traded/long/entry/exit/pnl with open=adr=upper=lower=stop=0, sessions=0). The instance that rolled the day had started at 17:08, adopted the open position through case 3/4 and returned before TryComputeLevels ever ran, so m_day.levels stayed empty. Harmless for trading, but such a row is a FAIL_levels for s021_parity.py. Fix later: compute the levels for the record when adopting a position on a day the instance did not start.

ALGODEV-62 phase C: taught the shared AlgoCore order layer to rest LIMIT orders, which is how S004 reproduces its inside-the-bar fill at the FVG zone edge live. The pending-order collectors are now parameterised by kind flags (S021 rests on stops, S004 on limits) and CTradeOps gained PlaceLimit. Added compile.sh, which builds every repo .mq5 in a throwaway terminal -- the live terminal is trading and must never be compiled into -- and moved the wine/terminal discovery plus the sandbox helpers into _mt5_env.sh, shared with run_selftest.sh. run_selftest.sh now compiles from the repo instead of running whatever .ex5 was deployed. All six .mq5 build clean and the S004 self-test still reports 12132/0.

Added the S004 live MQL5 layer (Runtime.mqh + EA shell) for ALGODEV-62 phase C. It parks one resting limit per symbol on the zone Engine.mqh would take next, keeps out-of-session and over-cap trades virtual so they still consume their zone, and replays warmup bars on restart instead of persisting state. TradeOps gained Modify() to retarget SL/TP after a gap fill. All .mq5 compile clean; self-test 12132/0.

Added mt5/tools/s021_manual.py so Anton can trade S021 by hand on an account the EA does not run on. No quote synchronisation is needed: only the session open is broker-specific, while the bands and the stop are distances off ADR14, which is the same underlying index's daily range at every broker. ADR14 is read from the newest 'levels' event in the EA log (written 09:30:10 New York daily, so current by construction), --adr overrides it when the EA is down. Position size is deliberately not computed -- contract units differ per platform. Verified against the live 2026-10-06 trade: U 31331.36 / SL 31080.65 reproduced exactly. SETUP.md sec 7.2 documents the manual OCO/cutoff/time-exit duties the EA would otherwise handle. tests/mt5: 47 passed.

Added mt5/tools/s021_capital.py: a standalone S021 order-price calculator that needs neither MT5 nor the EA. Started before the open it resolves the New York open itself (DST-aware), waits, derives ADR14 from MINUTE_5 session ranges over the engine's 09:30-15:59 window, reads the 09:30 open, prints and exits. Credentials via .env (CAPITAL_*), demo endpoint by default, read-only. Rejected a free index feed for the open after measuring 493 sessions (yfinance ^NDX vs the IC Markets USTEC export): the index open sits -34..+41 points from the broker's at 5-95% against a ~67-point band half-width, because the cash index is stale at 09:30:00 while constituents open; ADR14 by contrast carries across feeds with a stable -2.2% bias (sd 1.0%). Levels geometry and the by-hand checklist now live once, in s021_manual.print_plan. tests/mt5: 70 passed.

Added utils/telegram.py, a minimal shared HTML sender (token and chat id from the environment, send() returns False when unconfigured so Telegram stays optional). Both S021 manual tools gained --telegram via a shared deliver() helper; telegram_message() puts every order price in its own tap-to-copy <code> span. HTML parse mode rather than MarkdownV2 because the payload is mostly decimal numbers, which MarkdownV2 would require escaping outside code spans. The source label is html-escaped. tests/mt5 + tests/utils: 77 passed.

utils/telegram.py gained a setup helper: `python -m utils.telegram` lists the chat ids seen in getUpdates and sends a test message, so the fiddliest step of wiring a bot needs no manual API call. Pinned the dotenv path to the repo root instead of dotenv's stack-walking find_dotenv(), which raises AssertionError under `python -c` and stdin where there is no caller frame. Live-verified end to end against @anton_algo_desk_bot: getMe ok, chat id discovered, test message and a real S021 plan both delivered. tests: 77 passed.

ALGODEV-62 phase D: parity harness for the S004 live layer. mt5/tools/s004_parity.py diffs the EA's own trade list against strategies/fvg_mtf.run_backtest re-run on the broker's M1 exports (server tz -> UTC -> session clock, M1->M15 resample, hour filter then the portfolio daily cap), and classifies every row as match / ea_missed_fill / ea_halted (non-fatal, live-only outcomes) or FAIL_missing|extra|fields|status (exit 1). It re-runs the backtest with the EA's OWN pip and spread (new pip/cost columns in the CSV) because S004's Python data is in MT points, so modelled 0.9-pip costs would fake a mismatch in entry/sl/tp and in R. Three Runtime.mqh fixes the harness exposed: (1) no machine-readable trade list existed -- added FlushTradeRow/TradesCsvPath plus ResetTradesCsvForTester so a tester pass starts from an empty file in the append-only common folder; (2) `taken` was gated on trade_enabled, so a shadow pass would never spend the daily cap -- now taken = in_session && has_slot && !halted, the cap is spent BEFORE the fill check (a missed fill consumes its slot, the conservative choice that keeps the EA aligned with the backtest's cap), and each outcome records a S004_STATUS_* (taken/shadow/missed_fill/virtual_hour/virtual_cap/virtual_halt); (3) the engine was fed raw SERVER-time bars while S004 is defined on the Europe/Bucharest session clock -- new ServerToClock() converts on the way into Feed()/Warmup()/ParkLimit()/AdoptPositions, so the Asia window and the day roll match the backtest even in the weeks the US and EU DST calendars disagree (the ALGODEV-61 bug class). Order plumbing stays on the server clock. New input InpWriteTradesCsv; Engine.mqh exposes Cost() next to Pip(). Added Presets/AlgoTrading/S004_tester_shadow.set (InpTradeEnabled=false) and the shadow-pass procedure in mt5/README.md. compile.sh: 6/6 clean; run_selftest.sh: 12132 passed / 0 failed / 1102 trades (unchanged); tests/mt5 62 passed; full pytest 713 passed; ruff clean. The tester pass itself is NOT run here -- the sandbox would log a second terminal into the same FundingPips account where S021 trades; left to the maintainer.

Live-verified mt5/tools/s021_capital.py against Capital.com. Gotcha documented: an API key generated on the live platform returns HTTP 401 error.null.accountId on the demo host, so CAPITAL_DEMO=0 is required when no demo account exists. Epic confirmed as US100 (US Tech 100). Cross-checked the feed against the IC Markets USTEC export over 12 sessions: opens differ by -1.3 points on average (worst 8.9), session ranges by 3.6 on ~322, and ADR14 for 2026-10-06 was 337.1 vs the EA's 334.3 (0.9%). For contrast the free ^NDX index feed misses the open by -34..+41 points, so broker-fed open remains mandatory while ADR14 is portable.

ALGODEV-62: settled how the two legs on one prop account control risk, and wrote the answer down where it cannot be undone by accident. The DAILY limit needs no machinery -- risk_pct * max_trades_per_day already is a hard planned worst day (a full stop costs exactly 1R), and the two legs are sized so their sum clears the firm's -5%. The OVERALL limit is the one arithmetic says nothing about, so new backtest/run_s004_guard_modes.py measured every policy for it on identical bootstrapped paths: no guard, halt, and scale-the-size-to-the-remaining-room, at two thresholds (a whole planned day of room vs one trade's). No guard wins by 5-20x: median +23,859 over 3y at 6.98 breaches, against +827 for halting and +4,723 for sizing down, and the guarded accounts are dead 70-90% of their days. The reason is structural, not a parameter choice: any rule that stops sizing near the limit is ABSORBING -- with no trades the equity cannot move, the room never reopens, and the account ends without ever breaching anything, while a breach costs one $100 fee and restarts the challenge. Same result under the 1.15x slippage stress. Both guard inputs were already 0.0, so nothing changed in behaviour; what changed is that the zero is now documented as the decision, with the numbers, and with the condition that would flip it (a breach ceasing to be cheap: higher fee, limited retries, or a funded account whose status is worth more than a restart). Also recorded the setup trap found while checking this: AccountGuardRealizedSince reads the WHOLE account's deal history with no magic filter, so if a guard is ever enabled, each EA needs the firm's real limit, never 'its share' -- otherwise the two legs halt each other twice too early. compile 7/7 clean.

An unmatched selector exits 2 with the list of programs instead of deploying nothing. Fixed a latent bug on the way: 'selected_sources | grep -q' returns false under 'set -o pipefail' because grep -q closes the pipe early. Deployed S004 to the live terminal and verified S021_ORB.ex5 kept its md5 (d5cb5dd7) and mtime.

change: ExportM1 takes a symbol list; s004_parity filters foreign symbols and aligns the engine's history with the EA's warmup
why: First real shadow tester pass of phase D (FundingPips-SIM1, 2025.07.09-2026.10.04, 2218 EA trades). It exposed two defects in the harness itself: the shared exports folder still held S021's USTEC, which the engine happily traded and which then ate daily-cap slots (394 false FAIL_missing), and the engine was fed 500 days of bars against the EA's 1000-bar warmup, so it carried zones the EA never had (11 more).
details: ExportM1 now splits InpSymbol on commas, so one launch covers all seven pairs. s004_parity narrows bars to S004_INTRADAY.pairs, hard-fails when a pair the EA traded has no bars, warns when a configured pair is idle, and takes --ea-start/--warmup-bars to trim each frame positionally to the EA's own history. Result: 2182 match, 36 FAIL_status, 0 field divergences -- Engine.mqh reproduces fvg_mtf.py exactly on broker bars.

change: cap_tie: a swapped daily-cap slot is a known live-only outcome, not a parity failure
why: The first shadow pass left 36 FAIL_status rows over 18 days. The backtest breaks a tie by symbol name because it sorts ["time_in", "symbol"]; the EA reacts to each symbol's own closed M15 bar, so a pair whose bar lands one poll later has already lost the slot (log: EURUSD+USDCHF at 00:15:00, AUDUSD at 00:15:40). Owner's decision: accept and document rather than add a barrier in Poll(), which would delay entries into the next bar and cost real fills to match an ordering that is an artefact of the backtest's sort, not a rule of the strategy. Measured cost over 15 months: -1.71R taken against +12.73R the backtest took -- a sign that is luck, not bias.
details: s004_parity._reclassify_cap_ties() post-processes the report: inside one day, as many trades demoted to virtual_cap as promoted out of it become cap_tie. An unbalanced day means the EA spent the wrong number of slots and still fails (test_a_cap_the_ea_got_wrong_fails asserts it is not reclassified). The shadow pass now exits 0: 2182 match, 36 cap_tie, 0 field divergences. Params.mqh/gen_params, Runtime.mqh (Init and Poll comments) and mt5/README.md no longer claim the live layer orders ties by symbol name -- it only does so among the symbols whose bar closed in the same poll pass.

change: the manual S021 signal is sent by GitHub Actions, not by a process on the laptop
why: mt5/tools/s021_capital.py had to be started by hand before every session and kept the Mac awake until the open; a sleeping laptop meant a late message or none. The job is a natural fit for a hosted runner: it is stateless, needs no broker terminal, and finishes in minutes. Honest limitation accepted over a VPS: GitHub does not bound scheduling delay and may drop a scheduled run under load, so a missed day is possible. A delay is harmless (the wait absorbs it, and after the open the 09:30 bar is history), a drop costs that day's signal.
details: One UTC cron line (5 13 * * 1-5) rather than two seasonal ones: GitHub's scheduler knows nothing about DST, but the tool's own wait_for_open() does, so the job fires before the earliest possible open (13:30 UTC under EDT) and waits for the real one -- the same reasoning that gave the S021 entry in deployment/schedule.yml its `tz: UTC` plus wide window. timeout-minutes 120 covers the winter case (~85 min of waiting) without inheriting the 6-hour default. Installs requests + python-dotenv only, not requirements.txt: this path imports a frozen dataclass config and nothing heavier. CAPITAL_DEMO=0 is in the workflow, not in secrets -- it selects a host, and the comment next to it records why the demo host 401s. Verified before commit: the YAML parses, and `python -m mt5.tools.s021_capital --search nasdaq` exits 0 from a directory where no .env is reachable, i.e. on environment variables alone. A US holiday fails the run on purpose.

why: S004 is about to go on a chart next to S021 on account 21007756, and the 15 inputs were being typed by hand from the shadow preset -- which carries InpTradeEnabled=false and InpTimerSeconds=60, so a copy of it would have run silently without trading. 0.5% rather than the researched 1.0% is deliberate: run_s004_risk_grid prices the strategy's own trade-off (cap 2: 1.0% -> 6.98 busts/3y and a +23,859 median, 0.5% -> 3.18 busts and +14,920), but the reason for 0.5 is implementation risk, not strategy risk -- the shadow pass proved the decisions and never filled a real order, so slippage and missed limit fills are unmeasured. change: S004 verifies the broker timezone rule at init and halts on a mismatch
why: Attaching S004 live showed the checklist was asking the operator to confirm InpServerTzRule against server_offset_expected_s/observed_s -- fields only S021 logs. S004 had neither the check nor the fields, so a wrong rule failed silently: the bars still arrive, they are just labelled with the wrong hour, and the Asia entry window (00:00-06:59 on S004's own Europe/Bucharest clock) moves. That is the ALGODEV-61 class of bug, and it is live now: the EU changes clocks on 25 Oct and the US on 1 Nov, so the broker's EET_US_DST and the strategy's EET_EU_DST disagree by an hour that week.
details: S004Settings gains verify_server_offset, wired from the new InpVerifyServerOffset input (default true). Runtime::Init compares ClockObservedServerOffsetSeconds() with ClockOffsetSecondsAtUtc(server_rule) -- both already in AlgoCore/Clock.mqh, same call S021 makes -- and sets m_halted with a reason on a mismatch, so entries become virtual_halt instead of wrong-hour real trades. Live-only: TimeGMT() is not real in the tester. The init event now also carries server_tz_rule, server_offset_expected_s, server_offset_observed_s, tester and halted, and is logged at ERROR with a follow-up `halted` event when the check fails. Both S004 presets set InpVerifyServerOffset=true.

change: s021_manual picks the newest levels event by DATE, not by account folder name
why: Checking today's by-hand plan against the live EA exposed it: latest_levels() did sorted(glob(...), reverse=True) over FULL paths, so the account number dominated the file date. On 2026-10-07 acct53084682 had been detached before the open (deinit reason 6 at 15:06) and its newest file held only yesterday's levels, while acct21007756 logged today's at 16:30 -- the tool printed ADR14 334.279 from 2026-10-06 instead of 308.148, i.e. bands and stops ~8% too wide, and its own 'NOT today' warning was the only hint. The existing test used a single account folder, so the ordering bug was invisible.
details: Sort key is now (path.name, path): the file name is events-YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl, so dates order first and the account folder only breaks ties among files of the same day -- a same-day file with no levels event still falls through to the next account. Regression test test_latest_levels_prefers_todays_session_over_a_higher_numbered_account reproduces the live two-account layout. Verified after the fix: `--open 30986.25` reproduces the EA's own order requests to the cent (U 31047.88 / SL 30816.77, L 30924.62 / SL 31155.73, stop distance 231.11). 74 tests in tests/mt5 pass.

change: s021_capital logs into Capital.com AFTER waiting for the open, not before
why: Checking the new GitHub Actions runner (s021_signal.yml) against the real worst case: a Capital.com session token lives 10 minutes (documented in CapitalSession's own docstring), but main() called connect() before wait_for_open() -- and that wait runs up to ~85 minutes in winter (the same number the workflow's timeout-minutes comment already budgets for). Every scheduled run under a real wait would have logged in, then sat idle until the token was long dead, and failed its first request (session_ranges) with HTTP 401 -- the plan would never reach Telegram. Invisible so far because every run to date used --no-wait (open already past, login and first request nearly simultaneous).
details: main() now waits first, then calls connect() -- --search still logs in immediately since it never waits. Regression test test_main_logs_in_after_waiting_for_the_open_not_before monkeypatches wait_for_open/connect/session_ranges/open_price/deliver and asserts the call order is [wait, connect]. 75 tests in tests/mt5 pass.

details: Created tools/ (with an __init__ docstring naming the boundary: no MT5/MQL5 dependency) and tests/tools/, git mv'd s021_capital.py and its test there. s021_manual.py stays in mt5/tools -- it reads the EA's own Wine-path log files, so it is genuinely MT5-specific -- and the cross-package import (`from mt5.tools.s021_manual import deliver, levels_from_adr`) is unchanged and correct. Updated every caller: .github/workflows/s021_signal.yml (python -m tools.s021_capital), mt5/README.md (moved the one-line pointer out of the mt5/tools/ listing into its own line under tools/s021_capital.py), mt5/docs/SETUP.md. change: S004 entry limit can be moved toward the bounce: new default-off engine flag entry_shift_pips, S004_INTRADAY now sets 1.0 pip, mirrored into the MT5 EA as input InpEntryShiftPips
why: The backtest fills on the first touch of the zone edge, which credits fills a real limit queue misses (and the missed ones are instant reversals, i.e. winners; for buys the ask-vs-bid-bars gap adds to it). Sensitivity run on S004_INTRADAY 7 pairs RR3 2022-03+: limit moved toward the bounce 0/0.2/0.5/1.0/2.0 pip -> +0.164/+0.168/+0.176/+0.151/+0.148 R per trade, 5/5 years; fill-only-on-pierce 0/0.2/0.5/1.0/2.0 pip -> +0.164/+0.149/+0.128/+0.065/-0.013. 1.0 pip chosen by the spread argument, not as the table's peak (the 0.5 bump is noise). Requested by Anton 2026-10-08. A half-zone stop was tested the same day and rejected (0.5 zone: +0.031 R, 3/5 years).
details: fvg_mtf.run_backtest(entry_shift_pips=0.0): the limit price is near edge + dir * shift, touch test and fill price use it, the stop stays behind the far edge so risk and the rr target grow with the shift. Default 0 -> S004_BASE regression still reproduces the frozen trade list (5018 trades, max|delta| 4.4e-16). s004_config: ENTRY_SHIFT_PIPS=1.0, MAX_ENTRY_SHIFT_PIPS=2.0 (validated in __post_init__), field entry_shift_pips, S004_INTRADAY_NOSHIFT keeps the pre-amendment preset, S004_INTRADAY_CAP1 re-based on it because its numbers were measured unshifted. gen_params exports S004_DEFAULT_ENTRY_SHIFT_PIPS and S004_MAX_ENTRY_SHIFT_PIPS (Params.mqh regenerated). Engine.mqh: Configure takes shift_pips, new EntryEdgeOf(), TryEnter touches/fills on it; Runtime.mqh parks and risk-checks the limit at EntryEdgeOf and logs entry_shift_pips in the init event; S004_FVG.mq5 gains InpEntryShiftPips (refuses outside 0..2); both S004 presets set InpEntryShiftPips=1.0. Fixtures meta carries shift_pips and S004_SelfTest passes it to Configure. s004_parity.py gets --entry-shift-pips (default = preset; the trades CSV does not record it, so a run with another input must say so). Tests: 5 new in tests/strategies/test_s004_intraday.py, gen_params test extended; tests/mt5 + S004 tests 72 passed. NOT DONE: the MQL5 side is uncompiled and the self-test not re-run (needs MetaEditor under Wine: mt5/tools/compile.sh, mt5/tools/run_selftest.sh); the research notes and emulator numbers were measured unshifted and are not recomputed; reports/s004_intraday_portfolio_trades.csv is stale for S004_INTRADAY. Known live risk: a buy limit above the ask is refused by the broker, which the shift makes more likely when the market sits within the shift of the edge at park time (shows as missed_fill).

change: Fixed a live sizing bug: every real S004 entry overnight (5 orders, 7 pairs) sized at the broker's 0.01 minimum lot regardless of risk_pct
why: LotsFor() passed a POINTS-COUNT stop distance (distance/point, so ALGO_MIN_STOP_POINTS=0.5 stays meaningful) to SizingLotsForRisk() together with SizingMoneyPerPointPerLot()'s RAW-PRICE-UNIT money value (S021's convention: it passes a raw price distance instead). Mixing the two inflated the implied per-step cost by 1/point -- 100000x on 5-digit pairs (EURUSD), 1000x on JPY pairs -- so every risk-sized lot computed near-zero and floored to the broker minimum. Found live via mt5/MQL5/Scripts/AlgoTrading/S004_SizingProbe.mq5 (new, one-shot, places nothing): all 7 S004_SYMBOLS printed money_per_point_per_lot off by exactly that factor, and ALL of last night's real fills were 0.01 lots independent of each pair's own pip value -- the signature of a dead branch, not a scaling error.
details: Added AlgoCore/Sizing.mqh::SizingMoneyPerPointPerLotForPointStep(money_per_price_unit_per_lot, point) -- pure arithmetic (money_per_price_unit_per_lot * point), no broker call, so it is unit-testable without a live symbol. S004_FVG's LotsFor() now wraps SizingMoneyPerPointPerLot() in it before calling SizingLotsForRisk(). S021_ORB is untouched (it already passes a raw price distance, the convention SizingMoneyPerPointPerLot() was written for) -- verified by re-running S021_SelfTest (12172 passed, 0 failed) and checking S021_ORB.ex5's md5 unchanged after deploy. Added 3 cases to S004_SelfTest.mq5 (TestSizingPointStepConversion): the two real FundingPips readouts (EURUSD, GBPJPY) and an end-to-end check that a 15-pip/$50-risk EURUSD stop sizes to ~0.33 lots, not 0.01. Full self-test 12510 passed/0 failed/1136 trades (3 more passed than the previous entry, the new cases); pytest tests/mt5 61 passed. Deployed S004 only (deploy.sh S004); S021_ORB.ex5 md5 confirmed unchanged before/after.
